method: Use unseasoned mince made from 100% skinless turkey breast, weighed raw. Commercial mixed-cut turkey mince is not the specified ingredient; ask the butcher for breast mince or mince skinless breast at home.
Wash and dry the lettuce and tomato. Shred the lettuce and slice the tomato; put both on a clean plate, separate from the raw filling.
Warm the wholemeal flatbread in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 30–60 seconds on each side, until flexible. Keep it covered on a clean plate.
Mix the measured light mayonnaise and wholegrain mustard in a clean small bowl. Keep this finishing sauce separate from the uncooked filling and refrigerated until assembly.

Press the turkey breast mince firmly into three short koftas, each no thicker than 1.5cm; no skewers or binder are needed. Coat with all the measured black pepper. After handling raw turkey breast mince, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Heat the measured olive oil in the non-stick frying pan. Cook the turkey koftas over a medium heat for about 10–12 minutes, turning them onto every side. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Put the lettuce and tomato on the warm flatbread. Add the cooked turkey koftas and the cold finishing sauce, fold the bread around the filling and serve immediately.
